Reproduce the verification, from packages/contracts, with no key:
It returns true only when all nine wired slots agree from both ends, both
Settlement signature topics match what this repository computes, and both Bond

EvmV1Decoder.note: Pinned third-party decoding library. Five link references in SettlementVerifier resolve to this address; verified embedded in the deployed bytecode. Reused unchanged across the 2026-09-06 redeploy; it is a pure library with no wiring.

ServiceRegistry.note: Reused unchanged across the 2026-09-06 redeploy. It references TabBook, Bond and SettlementVerifier nowhere and takes only the curation authority in its constructor, so the Service registration, collections, emitters, prices and the queued curation change all survived.

AgentRegistry.redeployReason: tasks 10.12 and 12.6, two money defects in the previous deployment

Bond.redeployReason: tasks 10.12 and 12.6, two money defects in the previous deployment

TabBook.redeployReason: tasks 10.12 and 12.6, two money defects in the previous deployment
TabBook.note: Redeployed 2026-09-06 carrying the task 12.6 fix: a Metered Delivery spends prepaid credit before it raises the Open Tab, so banked credit is spendable rather than stranded. Redeployed together with AgentRegistry and Bond because the wiring setters are one-shot.

SettlementVerifier.note: Redeployed 2026-09-06 carrying the task 10.12 fix: a Transfer that a TabSettled in the same receipt already accounts for is skipped, so one payment is credited once. Proven on chain by re-submitting the transaction that returned ingestedLogs = 2 against the old verifier and getting 1.
SettlementVerifier.redeployReason: tasks 10.12 and 12.6, two money defects in the previous deployment

wiring.$comment: Five one-shot slots. Each reverts AlreadyWired once non-zero, so this table is final.

wiringAuthority.note: The deploying account. Its entire power over the rail was the ability to mis-wire it once, in public, at deployment; all five slots are now non-zero so that power is spent. Deliberately not the Watcher.

curationAuthority.note: A ServiceRegistry constructor argument, never settable afterwards. Gates Credit Limit weight only: no power over metering, tabs, or Bonds. The multisig below takes this role at the next deployment of ServiceRegistry, which is the only moment it can change.

watcher.note: May apply Provisional Clearings and report reorganisations. Cannot mint credit: a Provisional Clearing is covered by Bond and is revocable for its whole life.

curationMultisig.note: A 2-of-3 CurationMultisig, deployed 2026-09-08 and read back off chain. It holds no role on the live registry and cannot be given one: ServiceRegistry takes its authority as a constructor argument and exposes no setter, so the role moves only at a deployment. Recorded here because the contract is real and checkable, and because the address a future deployment will name should be public before that deployment rather than after it. It holds no value: there is no receive and no payable function anywhere in it.

bond.note: Verified as CollectionKind.Bond on both chains. Without this record no proven deposit can create stake, every Credit Limit stays at zero, and the rail is inert while appearing healthy.

0x10619F16E1ac73AAe41AA4C1619f1387687EED.note: Authorised on chainKey 1 alone, and verified unauthorised on chainKey 3. The mask is 1 << 1 exactly.

TabSettlement.note: The only contract Tab deploys to a Source Chain. No owner, no admin, no upgrade path, holds no balances and no tab state. It shares its address with EvmV1Decoder on Creditcoin because CREATE derives from sender and nonce, and the same deployer was at nonce 0 on both chains.

contracts.$comment: None, deliberately. On Mainnet a plain USDC Transfer to a registered Collection Address is the Settlement, so Tab deploys nothing here and reads only.
